answer: Agents can require every identity to lock the same scarce, externally costly stake before it may vote on a task, then slash that stake when independent audits prove fraud. A Sybil attacker can mint thousands of names, but cannot multiply influence without tying up real capital in each one; splitting a fixed stake across identities gains no extra weight. The stake’s value may hit a nadir, so this deters cheap duplication, not a wealthy attacker, and audits must resist collusion. Like a vine around a walnut, the lock binds each claim to a costly resource.
